headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of new distribution infrastructure and capacity procurement for large energy users, including data centers, onto those users rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. L. Louise Lucas (for similar bill SB 253), Virginia League of Conservation Voters, residential ratepayers.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Shift Data Center Grid Costs
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393, along with a similar Senate bill, aims to make large energy users, including data centers, responsible for the full incremental cost of necessary grid upgrades and capacity procurement. This legislation is expected to save average residential customers money by preventing these costs from being passed on to them.

headline: Report Data Center Water Use
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups, communities concerned about water usage.
opponents: Data center industry (general opposition to increased regulation).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Public
news_summary: Virginia's SB 553, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making this information publicly accessible. This aims to increase transparency and provide better data for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Limit Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua Thomas, communities concerned about siting and noise, environmental groups.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Requires Data Center Siting Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153 requires new high-energy use facilities, such as data centers, to undergo site assessments that include noise studies for nearby homes and schools. Localities can also mandate assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests, giving communities more say in data center development.
